installation.note: gunzip is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: The gunzip command decompresses files that were compressed with gzip. It's essentially the same as 'gzip -d' but with a more intuitive name for decompression. It removes the .gz extension and restores the original file.
when_to_use: Decompress files downloaded from the internet
Decompress files for editing or processing

syntax.description: Decompress one or more .gz files. By default, gunzip replaces the compressed file with the decompressed version. If no files are specified, gunzip reads from stdin.

misconceptions.title: gunzip is different from gzip -d
misconceptions.misconception: gunzip and gzip -d are different commands with different features
misconceptions.reality: gunzip is exactly the same as 'gzip -d'. They are aliases - use whichever name you prefer.
misconceptions.tip: gunzip and gzip -d are identical - choose based on which name is clearer for your use case

misconceptions.title: gunzip extracts archives
misconceptions.reality: gunzip only decompresses .gz files. For .tar.gz archives, use 'tar -xzf archive.tar.gz' to extract the archive.
misconceptions.tip: Use tar -xzf for .tar.gz files, gunzip only handles .gz compression

common_pitfalls.description: Forgetting -k flag causes .gz files to be deleted after extraction
common_pitfalls.solution: Use -k flag when you need to keep the compressed archive: gunzip -k file.gz

common_pitfalls.description: gunzip file.tar.gz creates file.tar, but doesn't extract the tar archive
common_pitfalls.solution: Use tar -xzf archive.tar.gz to extract both compression and archive, or gunzip then tar -xf

common_pitfalls.description: gunzip only works on .gz files, not .zip, .bz2, or other formats
common_pitfalls.solution: Use appropriate tools: unzip for .zip, bunzip2 for .bz2, gunzip for .gz

related_commands.relationship: Compression; gzip compresses, gunzip decompresses (gunzip = gzip -d)
Archiving; often used with gunzip to extract compressed archives
Alternative extraction; unzip handles .zip files, gunzip handles .gz files

best_practices: Use -k to keep compressed files when needed: gunzip -k file.gz
Use -t to test files before decompressing large archives
Use -c to extract to different filenames or pipe to other commands
Use -r for batch extraction of compressed files in directories
For .tar.gz files, use tar -xzf instead of gunzip + tar
performance_tips: gunzip is very fast for decompression
Test files with -t before decompressing to avoid wasting time on corrupted files
Use -c for streaming decompression when piping to other commands

additional_notes.equivalence: gunzip is identical to 'gzip -d' - they are the same command
additional_notes.file_replacement: By default, .gz files are removed after decompression. Use -k to keep them.
additional_notes.archive_format: gunzip only handles .gz compression. For .tar.gz, use tar -xzf.
additional_notes.stdin_support: gunzip can read from stdin: cat file.gz | gunzip > output.txt
